chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

We sent to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while we were a group in Medina, saying that we wish to bid you farewell. He sent back to us: 'Bathe in Medina, for I fear that water may become scarce for you at Dhi al-Hulayfah, so bathe in Medina and wear the garments in which you will enter the state of Ihram, then come to me individually or in pairs.'

And this narration does not contradict what we mentioned regarding the permissibility of wearing the qamis (shirt) until reaching the Miqat, because if one acts upon this, he is not burdened by it; and if he wears the qamis until reaching the Miqat and then puts on his two Ihram garments, he is not bound by anything else either.

key_terms.اَلْقَمِيصِ: The shirt (a specific garment worn by men)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing the ritual bath for Hajj at the Miqat versus in Medina according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advised his companions to perform ghusl in Medina rather than at Dhi al-Hulayfah to avoid water scarcity, illustrating the principle of *rukhsah* (concession) in ritual purity. The accompanying juristic commentary reconciles this with the general permissibility of wearing the qamis until the Miqat, demonstrating the flexibility within Shia fiqh where specific instructions do not necessarily abrogate general rulings but offer alternative valid practices.
